caption:
Dad says he needs nothing? Tell AI what he loves and your budget, and ask for 5 gift ideas, one line each.

AI, for real · Day 11. One real test of what AI can do, with the output shown.

WHY IT WORKS: "he has everything" is a blank page. AI connects what he already enjoys (gardening, crosswords, black coffee) to things at your price, so you start from a short list instead of an endless shopping page.

THE REAL TEST (Dad is made up for this post):
Prompt: "Help me pick a gift for my dad. He's 64, loves gardening and crossword puzzles, drinks his coffee black, and says he doesn't need anything. My budget is $40. Give me 5 ideas, one line each."
Claude's 5 ideas (headings and prices word for word; it added a short reason to each):
1. Premium whole-bean coffee sampler (~$30)
2. Quality garden pruners (~$35)
3. New York Times crossword book plus a nice pen (~$25)
4. Heirloom seed collection (~$25)
5. Personalized garden kneeler or stool (~$40)
Its top pick, word for word: "For a "doesn't need anything" dad, the seeds or the coffee usually work best, because they get used up and won't add clutter."

THE CATCH: the prices are AI estimates, not live prices, and it can't check what's in stock near you. Check the price where you'd actually buy it.

PRIVACY TIP: their likes and your budget are all it needs. Leave out full names, addresses and health details.

Do this: in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, type "Help me pick a gift for my dad. He's 64, loves gardening and crossword puzzles, drinks his coffee black, and says he doesn't need anything. My budget is $40. Give me 5 ideas, one line each." Change the person, age, likes and budget to yours.

Send this to whoever you're splitting Dad's gift with.

AI, for real · Day 12 is Wednesday at 5:45 pm.

Follow to learn one real AI trick a day.
